Dominickers.subject: Indian Architecture
Dominickers.question: What do you know about The Dominickers?
Dominickers.answer: a small biracial ethnic group located within the Florida Panhandle, centered near the town of Ponce de Leon in Holmes Co
Dominickers.fact: The Dominickers were a small biracial ethnic group located within the Florida Panhandle, centered near the town of Ponce de Leon in Holmes County, Florida. The group became well known locally, to the extent that Dominicker and Dominickers became regional terms for people of mixed race.

Dominickers.subject: Indian Architecture
Dominickers.question: Members of the group descended from a single interracial marriage during the _____ period, and were of generationally mixed African American and European American ancestry
Dominickers.fact: Members of the group descended from a single interracial marriage during the Antebellum period, and were of generationally mixed African American and European American ancestry.

Dominickers.subject: Indian Architecture
Dominickers.question: During the 20th century, academics classified them among 200 presumed "racial isolates" along groups such as the _____ and Melungeons
Dominickers.fact: During the 20th century, academics classified them among 200 presumed "racial isolates" along groups such as the Redbones and Melungeons. The Redbones of Southwest Louisiana, who the Dominickers were mapped as residing nearby to, were sometimes called Dominics.

Dominickers.subject: Indian Architecture
Dominickers.question: She married him during the first years of the _____, and they later had five children together
Dominickers.fact: She married him during the first years of the Civil War, and they later had five children together.

Dominickers.subject: Indian Architecture
Dominickers.question: Said children married both _____ and white spouses, and their descendants rose in number over time
Dominickers.fact: According to local accounts, the name derives from a divorce case in which a local man described his estranged wife as "black and white, like an old Dominicker chicken." Over time, both "Dominicker" and "Dominickers" evolved into generalized racial terms within the region in reference to all people of mixed African and European ancestry. Said children married both Black and white spouses, and their descendants rose in number over time.
